backups.invalid_reason: accidental production side-effect during the G1-iter5-i2 CLOSING fix cycle (the fifth incident of the class, a NEW variant): the orchestrator's mutC mutation probe (relative-refusal removed) patched PROD_CHECKOUT to a scratch stand-in in the mutated copy — per the seq-10 rule — but did NOT patch the TEST LANES that reference the real production path. With the constant patched, the real-path lanes no longer matched anything and were NOT refused: the guard test's push-target lanes pushed a scratch lineage INTO the production checkout (the divergence self-heal then merged it — a -s ours merge and manifest union, exactly as designed, on the wrong base; this entry and its siblings are that lineage), and the override test's symlink REPO lane executed a full backup directly against the production checkout. Patching the guarded constant ALONE NEUTRALIZES the guard for every lane that still references the real path — the correct rule (now recorded): patch BOTH SIDES, the constant AND every test lane that references the real protected path, or run guard-mutation probes only where the production path does not exist. Content verified clean: all scan layers ran in every involved run; the manifest union followed the documented triple-key semantics; the production checkout's working tree was never touched (only its local branch ref). Audit-trail pollution only. Disclosed in the G1-iter5 record amendment, README anomaly log, lessons, and the post-closure session log.
